questions.q: What is the primary purpose of ongoing evaluation?
options: To set goals
To explore ideas
To establish consumer needs
To solve design issues as they arise
questions.explanation: Ongoing (formative) evaluation happens throughout the design process so problems can be identified and resolved as they emerge, keeping the project on track. Setting goals and establishing needs occur at the start of the process, not as part of continuous evaluation.

questions.q: A manufacturer chooses to produce cutting boards made from bamboo because it can be regrown and is inexpensive. Which of the following would be the manufacturer's determining factor when selecting this material?
options: Aesthetics
Availability
Sustainability
Life cycle analysis
questions.explanation: Choosing a material because it can be regrown points to sustainability — using a renewable resource that can be replenished for future use. Availability only concerns whether the material can be obtained, not the renewable, environmentally responsible reasoning given here.

questions.q: What is the most important factor for a designer to consider when developing an innovation with ergonomic features?
options: Ensuring the product is user friendly
Integrating the latest emerging technology
Finding a reliable manufacturer to efficiently develop the product
Providing end users with resources to develop an understanding of the technology
questions.explanation: Ergonomics is about fitting a product to the human user, so the key consideration is that the product is comfortable, safe and user friendly. Emerging technology and manufacturing reliability are separate concerns unrelated to the ergonomic fit between product and user.

questions.q: What are designers responding to when they develop products to assist people in society?
options: Emerging trends
Identified needs
Innovative processes
The natural resources available
questions.explanation: Designing products to assist people is a direct response to identified needs — the recognised problems or requirements of users that the design sets out to solve. Emerging trends may influence a design, but the underlying driver of products that assist society is a genuine identified need.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a work health and safety (WHS) risk assessment?
options: To identify dangerous equipment
To evaluate workshop organisation and practices
To access the impact of materials on the environment
To identify and assess potential injury or illness in the workplace
questions.explanation: A WHS risk assessment systematically identifies hazards and evaluates the potential for injury or illness so controls can be put in place. Identifying dangerous equipment is only one part of this broader process of assessing all workplace risks to people.

it is classified as an antique.
it cannot be repaired because parts are not available.
a variety of materials is considered during design and development.
questions.explanation: Obsolescence means a product is no longer useful or supportable — for example when it cannot be repaired because parts are no longer available, forcing replacement. Merely ageing does not make a product obsolescent if it still functions and can be maintained.

questions.q: Which of the following is most important for an innovative idea to be successful?
options: A comprehensive marketing plan
Workload management and state of the art equipment
Thorough planning, research, timing and consumer demand
Using local and current technologies for immediate release in the marketplace
questions.explanation: Successful innovation depends on thorough planning and research, good timing and genuine consumer demand — without a real market need even a well-marketed idea fails. A marketing plan alone cannot make a product succeed if these underlying factors are not met.

questions.q: What is the purpose of securing protection of intellectual property?
options: To guarantee ownership of the domain name
To prevent others from creating a similar product
To prevent breach or violation of trademarks, patents and copyright
To provide a legal framework to protect a designer's creative ideas and designs
questions.explanation: Intellectual property protection exists to give designers a legal framework that protects their original creative ideas and designs, recognising them as the owner. Trademarks, patents and copyright are the specific mechanisms within that framework rather than the overall purpose itself.

questions.q: Which of the following describes a product life cycle analysis?
options: An overview of the environmental impact at the development phase
An assessment of the manufacturer's costs to transport and distribute the product
The examination of the extraction, manufacturing and final disposal of the product
The determination of how materials for the product will be extracted and processed
questions.explanation: A life cycle analysis examines a product across its entire life — from raw material extraction through manufacturing to final disposal. The other options describe only a single stage, whereas an LCA assesses the whole cradle-to-grave journey.

questions.q: Which of the following best demonstrates a designer taking an ethical approach when creating a new product?
options: Developing a product that avoids excessive use of resources
Using innovative technologies to ensure greater uptake in the marketplace
Targeting the aspirations of clients to develop a product that is easier to use
Adapting procedures to protect the rights and responsibilities of the designer
questions.explanation: An ethical approach considers responsibility to society and the environment, such as avoiding the excessive use of resources to reduce waste and environmental harm. The other options focus on marketability or the designer's own interests rather than ethical responsibility to the wider community and environment.

questions.q: Outline ONE factor that could affect the success or failure of a design.

criteria.descriptor: Outlines a factor that could affect the impact on the success or failure of a design

questions.modelAnswer: One important factor is functionality — how well a product, system or environment performs its intended purpose. If the design fails to perform its intended function efficiently, it may result in design failure. (Other valid factors include the appropriateness of the design solution, needs, aesthetics, finance/cost, ergonomics, obsolescence and time.)

questions.q: How has ONE social trend led to a higher demand for innovative solutions?

criteria.descriptor: Demonstrates a thorough understanding of how a social trend has led to a higher demand for innovative solutions
Demonstrates an understanding of how a social trend has led to a higher demand for innovative solutions

questions.modelAnswer: The desire to be in constant contact with others has increased the demand for devices that communicate in a variety of formats. These platforms allow individuals to communicate anytime, anywhere around the world. (Other valid trends include the growth of social influencers shaping design directions; the use of innovation and current technologies for education, entertainment and communication such as social media; and rising environmental awareness and government legislation, e.g. bans on single-use plastic bags, containers and cutlery.)

questions.q: Explain the advantages of ONE communication technique that could be used when presenting information to a client.

criteria.descriptor: Provides an explanation of the advantages of ONE communication technique that could be used when presenting information to a client
Demonstrates an understanding of the advantages of ONE communication technique that could be used when presenting information to a client
Demonstrates understanding of the advantage(s) of ONE communication technique

questions.modelAnswer: Interactive prototyping can improve client communication. A tangible model or digital simulation lets the client interact with the proposed design, experiencing its functionality, usability and aesthetics and helping them understand its benefits. This hands-on approach improves communication, reduces misunderstandings and allows clients to provide valuable feedback, resulting in better design decisions and a better outcome.

questions.q:
Technology has improved the lifestyle for many. However, it has come at a cost to society and the environment.

Discuss this statement in relation to ONE technology.

criteria.descriptor: Provides a thorough discussion of ONE technology; makes thorough reference to society and the environment; makes reference to lifestyle improvement
Provides a sound discussion of ONE technology; makes sound reference to society and the environment; makes reference to lifestyle improvement
Provides a discussion of ONE technology; makes reference to cost to society OR the environment OR lifestyle improvements
Demonstrates some understanding of a technology in relation to the statement

questions.modelAnswer: The impact of modern transportation exemplifies the dual nature of technology. While it has enhanced our lifestyles with greater accessibility and convenience, it has also posed significant challenges to society and the environment. The proliferation of automobiles has revolutionised personal mobility, connecting people and places like never before. However, this convenience has contributed to issues such as traffic congestion, air pollution and the depletion of fossil fuels. Therefore, while technology has improved our lives in various ways, its implementation demands thoughtful consideration of its consequences to mitigate negative effects and achieve sustainable progress.

questions.q:
Complex challenges require designers to be creative in addressing the ongoing needs of society.

Analyse the ethical and social implications for designers in creating solutions to world issues. In your response, refer to TWO of the following examples: Health, Food production, Living conditions.

Your answer will be assessed on how well you: demonstrate knowledge and understanding relevant to the question; communicate ideas and information using relevant examples; and present a logical and cohesive response.

criteria.descriptor: Provides a comprehensive analysis of the ethical and social implications for designers in the creation of solutions to world issues; provides a logical and cohesive response; communicates ideas and information using relevant examples; makes detailed reference to TWO alternate world issues facing designers

Provides some analysis of the ethical and social implications facing designers in the creation of solutions to world issues; provides mostly a logical and cohesive response; communicates information using examples; makes reference to TWO alternate world issues facing designers
Provides a sound understanding of the ethical and social implications facing designers in the creation of solutions to world issues; refers to alternate world issues facing designers
Demonstrates a basic understanding of the ethical and/or social implications facing designers in the creation of solutions to world issues

questions.modelAnswer: Addressing complex challenges in society requires designers to be creative in developing solutions, but when creating solutions to world issues such as health or living conditions, designers must also weigh the ethical and social implications of their designs. In health, the ethical implications include privacy and data security, equity and accessibility, and informed consent, while the social implications include health disparities, stigmatisation and discrimination, and cultural sensitivity. In living conditions, ethical concerns include government support (childcare, housing, medical), capping energy costs, faster introduction of greener technologies, fair wages and the safety, health and wellbeing of displaced communities, while the social implications include the diminishment of living standards, the impact of climate change, housing pressures (relocation, social housing, pop-up and transportable housing) and young adults living at home longer due to cost of living. A comprehensive response judges that by carefully considering these ethical principles and social wellbeing across two such issues, designers can create impactful solutions that meet the diverse needs of society while acting responsibly.
